was this a bug that was there all this time?
There is another call to refine to fix on [line 104](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/4199/files#diff-d23004038675fb0d352846b17da97790L104)

This is rather an internal method no?
It's only used within this class (in `pages`) so it can be private & static?
This looks like it could be private & static too since it's only used within this class?
this was a bug in the test, yes. I'll fix the other occurrance too.

I would have expected to read here, am I missing something?
```suggestion
  TPaginationWidgetParams
```
It seems like we should add an expectation with `toHaveBeenCalledWith(...)` to properly test the refine behavior then.

I would have expected this value to be casted as
```suggestion
      widgetParams || ({} as TPaginationWidgetParams);
```

```suggestion
   * Creates URLs for the next state, the number is the page to generate the URL for.
```

I would have prefered we include the refactoring of the tests before merging, because I sense it's the kind of thing we end up never doing.
Is there a reason (other than PR bloat) not to refactor them in this diff?
PR bloat and I wasn’t sure what the alternative way of testing this could be.
There's a type called `Unmounter`.
We can chain the calls.

```suggestion
            createURL: connectorState.createURL(helper.state),
```

```suggestion
            refine: connectorState.refine,
```

I agree with @tkrugg.

There's no need to test `widget.refine()` at the widget level. We should rather mount the widget and interact with it to trigger the expected behaviors.
I copied from QueryRules connector, meaning that that one is wrong too
After fully reviewing, this test doesn't make sense here in the end. See https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/4199#discussion_r349163769.
It's not wrong, it was introduced meanwhile.
